walkthroughs.body_html:
Britain: Health & the People c1000 to Present Day — a core area of GCSE History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Britain: Health & the People c1000 to Present Day brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

mcqs.q: Which event triggered Bazalgette's sewer system?
options: Cholera epidemic 1854
Great Stink 1858
Great Fire 1666
Typhoid outbreak 1860

mcqs.q: Why were 19th-century industrial cities so unhealthy?
options: Cities were unhealthy because Victorians did not care about hygiene.
Rapid population growth outpaced housing, water and sewage; lack of regulation produced overcrowded slums and cholera epidemics until reforms followed Chadwick's 1842 report.
Because Britain banned slavery before other countries.
Cities were unhealthy because factory smoke poisoned the food.

mcqs.q: Why was the NHS founded in 1948?
options: The NHS was founded because Churchill wanted to thank soldiers after WWII.
Beveridge's 1942 report identified disease as a 'giant evil'; Labour's 1945 manifesto promised universal healthcare; Bevan unified hospitals and made care free at point of use.
Because Britain banned slavery before other countries.
The NHS was founded in 1918 after the influenza pandemic.

mcqs.q: Why did the Industrial Revolution begin in Britain?
options: A combination of capital from trade and empire, coal and iron deposits, agricultural improvements, political stability, and a culture of invention.
Because James Watt invented the steam engine.
Because Britain banned slavery before other countries.
Cities were unhealthy because factory smoke poisoned the food.
